item.title: President Prabowo Attends National Christmas Celebration in Jakarta
item.description: Jakarta. President Prabowo Subianto on Monday evening attended the 2025 National Christmas Celebration at the Indoor Tennis Stadium in Senayan, Jakarta, conveying a message of tolerance and unity in Indonesia’s diverse society. The annual celebration, themed “God Is Present to Save the Family,” drew thousands of participants from across the country. item.title: Maduro Appears in US Court After Capture on Narco-Terrorism Charges
item.description: New York. Deposed Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro is set to make his first appearance Monday in an American courtroom on the narco-terrorism charges the Trump administration cited to justify capturing him and bringing him to New York. Maduro and his wife are expected to appear at noon before a judge for a brief but required legal proceeding that will likely mark the start of a prolonged legal battle over whether he can be put on trial in the United States. item.title: JCI Sets Fresh Intraday Record at Tuesday Open
item.description: Jakarta. Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) extended its rally at Tuesday’s open, rising 31 points, or 0.36%, to 8,890, as the benchmark continued to carve out fresh intraday record highs. The index traded in the range of 8,879–8,895 in early dealings, marking its latest all-time high during the session. Early trading activity remained active. item.title: Safe-Haven Rush Pushes Antam Gold Back Near Record Territory
item.description: Jakarta. Gold prices in Indonesia surged on Tuesday, with Antam bullion jumping Rp 34,000 to Rp 2,549,000 ($152.06) per gram, reflecting renewed global demand for safe-haven assets. Data from Logam Mulia showed the state miner’s gold had already climbed Rp 27,000 on Monday to Rp 2,515,000 per gram. The all-time high for Antam gold remains Rp 2,605,000 per gram, recorded on Dec. 27, 2025. item.description: Jakarta. item.title: Indonesia Rolls Out Import Safeguards to Shield Textile Industry
item.description: Jakarta. Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa has formally imposed safeguard duties on imports of cotton woven fabrics, with the measure set to take effect on Jan. 10, as the government moves to shield the domestic textile industry from a surge in imports. item.title: Saudi Tourist Killed as Jet Ski Capsizes in W. Java
item.description: Sukabumi, W. Java. A jet ski carrying two riders capsized after being struck by large waves at Bupalo Beach in Palabuhanratu, Sukabumi Regency, on Monday afternoon, killing a Saudi Arabian national and leaving another rider in critical condition, authorities said. item.title: Superflu in Indonesia: What the Public Needs to Know
item.description: Jakarta. The term superflu has gained attention amid rising influenza cases overseas. Health experts say it is not a new disease, but a public label commonly used for flu outbreaks linked to Subclade K, a new mutation of the Influenza A (H3N2) virus. Subclade K has been reported as a dominant strain in the United Kingdom, Japan, and parts of the United States. item.title: Cabinet Retreat to Focus on Food as Indonesia No Longer Imports Rice
item.description: Jakarta. President Prabowo Subianto is gathering his ministers for another cabinet retreat on Tuesday that will focus on food self-sufficiency, among others, as Indonesia no longer relies on foreign rice supplies. Shortly after Prabowo assumed power in late October 2024, the ex-army general took his cabinet members on a military-style retreat in Magelang.
